name: hero
whatItDemonstrates: A top navigation bar whose Overview and Handbook triggers open dropdown panels of link cards rendered through a portal with an arrow, while a third bar item is a plain external GitHub link.
stateManaged: none — fully uncontrolled; no value/defaultValue props anywhere, open-item state is managed internally by the root
nonTrivialInteractions: Content is authored inside each Item but is relocated into the portal Viewport (inside Portal > Positioner > Popup) when its item activates
Trailing caret Icon rotates 180° while its panel is open via data-popup-open
Content enter/leave transitions key off data-starting-style/data-ending-style and data-activation-direction (left/right) to slide toward the previously/currently active trigger

Positioner uses sideOffset={10}, collisionPadding={{top:5,bottom:5,left:20,right:20}} and collisionAvoidance={{side:'none'}}, and transitions top/left/right/bottom while moving between triggers; the Arrow repositions via data-[side]
A custom Link wrapper exercises the render prop (render={<a />}) as the documented seam for swapping in a framework router link; the GitHub bar item is a Link styled as a trigger

name: nested
whatItDemonstrates: A second-level NavigationMenu.Root nested inside the Overview panel's Content, where a card-style Handbook trigger opens its own right-side portal popup containing the handbook link cards.
stateManaged: none — both roots fully uncontrolled; no value/defaultValue props, the nested submenu opens only through trigger activation
nonTrivialInteractions: The nested Root (orientation="vertical", on the nested instance) sits in a plain <li> inside the parent Content with its own List > Item > Trigger > Content tree; no parent props are needed to enable nesting

The nested tree has its own Portal > Positioner > Popup > Viewport; the nested Positioner anchors side="right" align="end" with sideOffset={8} and alignOffset={-8} so the submenu popup lines up with the parent card
The nested Popup omits the Arrow while the top-level popup keeps one
The nested Trigger is a link-card button whose right-pointing caret rotates via data-popup-open

The top-level bar matches the hero treatment: icon rotation, activation-direction content slide, and collision padding on the top-level Positioner (sideOffset={10}, no collisionAvoidance in this demo)

name: nested-inline
whatItDemonstrates: A Product mega-menu whose panel hosts a second-level Root rendered without a Portal: a sidebar of audience submenus sits next to an inline Viewport so submenu content swaps in place, with the Developers item pre-opened and orientation flipping between vertical and horizontal at a 700px breakpoint.
stateManaged: uncontrolled — the nested inline Root passes defaultValue="developers" to pre-open that item on mount; orientation is derived from useMediaQuery('(min-width: 700px)', { defaultMatches: true }) rather than React state; no useState anywhere
nonTrivialInteractions: The nested Root renders only List + Viewport (no Portal/Positioner/Popup); its Viewport shares a two-column grid with the sidebar List so activated submenu content replaces the panel content in place

orientation={isDesktop ? 'vertical' : 'horizontal'} comes from useMediaQuery with defaultMatches: true for SSR, switching the submenu between a sidebar layout and a horizontal strip (orientation/defaultValue are on the nested instance)
Each nested Item passes an explicit value from the shared ../data audienceMenus module, and defaultValue="developers" pre-opens the Developers submenu
Submenu Content transitions use vertical activation-direction (up/down) slides plus a blur effect on desktop, while the top-level Content slides horizontally
The Learn panel renders a static guides panel with links from the shared data module, and the Releases/GitHub bar items are plain Links
The top-level Popup's ending style transitions only opacity and scale (data-ending-style:transition-[opacity,scale])
